### 02_jones_toffoli_measurement
# Toffoli with 4 T via measurement (Jones 2013)

**What it does.** Implements a full Toffoli `ccx(a, b, c)` with Clifford operations plus four T gates
instead of seven: compute `a AND b` into one clean ancilla (4 T), CNOT the ancilla onto `c`, then erase the
ancilla by X-basis measurement and a classically controlled CZ(a, b). Jones also shows that adding n
control inputs to a controlled gate costs 4n T (best prior 8n), and gives an error-detecting 8-T Toffoli
variant (post-selection suppresses error from 4p to 28p^2 to lowest order).

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Toffoli whose target is not a fresh ancilla (in-place targets, e.g.
the final Toffoli of a tof_n ladder, MAJ/UMA steps of a Cuccaro adder) when one clean ancilla is available.
Equivalent to card 01 used as compute + CNOT + uncompute.

**Cost.** 4 T, 1 clean ancilla, 1 measurement, 1 classically controlled CZ per Toffoli (vs 7 T, 0 ancillas).
T-depth can be 1 with the AND written in T-depth-one form (card 04).

**Verification mode: relaxed.** Uses an ancilla precondition and a measurement; check with the
specification contract (invariant 2), not unitary equality.

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`).** Standard Toffoli `ir._CCX`: 7 T, 6 CX,
distance 3e-33 to CCX (`toffoli_7T`). The 4-T AND gadget and its measurement uncompute are verified under
`temporary_and`; the Jones Toffoli is AND -> CX(anc, c) -> uncompute = 4 T (`jones_toffoli`, derived count).
In the suite: every ccz in tof_n / barenco_tof_n / adders is a candidate (MANIFEST.csv `ccx_count`).

**Citation.** C. Jones, "Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate",
*Phys. Rev. A* 87, 022328 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.87.022328, arXiv:1212.5069 (arXiv title: "Novel
constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate").

### 08_pyzx_zx_simplification
# ZX-calculus T-count reduction / phase teleportation (Kissinger & van de Wetering 2020)

**What it does.** Converts the circuit to a ZX-diagram, simplifies it to a graph-like normal form
(local complementation and pivoting remove interior Clifford spiders), gadgetizes phases so non-Clifford
phases on the same parity meet and fuse across Hadamards ("phase teleportation"), then extracts a circuit.
Phase teleportation does not change the number or location of non-phase gates; it also works with arbitrary
and symbolic phases. The same simplifier often proves the optimized circuit equal to the original.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T or Clifford+Rz circuit; strongest where Hadamards split phase
polynomials into regions that phase folding alone cannot merge (Toffoli-heavy arithmetic). It cannot
introduce ancillas or measurements, so it stays at the unitary T-count (e.g. 8n for ripple-carry adders).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count in our runs; no ancillas, no measurements. Extraction can increase CNOT
count (TKET / basic_optimization help).

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving). Self-check: `zx.Circuit.verify_equality`; the project
re-checks every output independently (dense unitary / statevector / sparse basis pairs).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/bench_runs/run2/`, pyzx 0.10.7, full_reduce -> extract_circuit ->
to_basic_gates -> basic_optimization).** tof_3: 21 -> 15 T; adder_8: 399 -> 173 T; cuccaro_4: 56 -> 32 T;
all verified against the input. The paper's Table 1 (arXiv:1903.10477v2 p.4) lists 15 for tof3 and 173 for
adder8 (PyZX column).

**Citation.** A. Kissinger, J. van de Wetering, "Reducing the number of non-Clifford gates in quantum
circuits", *Phys. Rev. A* 102, 022406 (2020), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.102.022406, arXiv:1903.10477 (arXiv title:
"Reducing T-count with the ZX-calculus").

### 07_phase_folding_tpar
# Phase folding and T-par (Amy, Maslov, Mosca 2014)

**What it does.** Inside a {CNOT, X, T, S, Z} region every phase gate applies omega^k to a parity (XOR of
input variables) of the region's inputs: the region is a phase polynomial plus a linear reversible map.
Terms on the same parity merge (T + T = S, T + T^dagger = I), which cuts T-count ("phase folding"); T-par then
re-synthesizes each region, grouping parities into T layers by matroid partitioning to minimize T-depth,
optionally with ancillas. Hadamard gates bound the regions.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T circuit with repeated parities across CNOT networks: expanded
Toffoli cascades (each 7-T Toffoli is 7 parity terms), adders, GF(2^n) multipliers, Hamming / hwb circuits.
Also on Clifford+Rz with arbitrary angles (merge angles on equal parities).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count; no ancillas or measurements for T-count reduction (ancillas only for
T-depth). Reported on its benchmarks: up to 65.7 % T-count and 87.6 % T-depth reduction without ancillae.

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving; D[omega] check of the rewritten window).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`, key `phase_folding_parity`).**
`cx(0,1) t(1) cx(0,1)` and `cx(1,0) t(0) cx(1,0)` both put T on parity x0+x1; the two terms fold into S on
that parity: 2 T -> 0 T (pyzx), dense-unitary distance 1e-16. The project already has a deterministic
phase-folding pass (`circuitevolve/blocks/passes.py`).

**Citation.** M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, "Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits
via matroid partitioning", *IEEE Trans. Comput.-Aided Des. Integr. Circuits Syst.* 33(10), 1476-1489 (2014),
doi:10.1109/TCAD.2014.2341953, arXiv:1303.2042.

### 02_jones_toffoli_measurement
# Toffoli with 4 T via measurement (Jones 2013)

**What it does.** Implements a full Toffoli `ccx(a, b, c)` with Clifford operations plus four T gates
instead of seven: compute `a AND b` into one clean ancilla (4 T), CNOT the ancilla onto `c`, then erase the
ancilla by X-basis measurement and a classically controlled CZ(a, b). Jones also shows that adding n
control inputs to a controlled gate costs 4n T (best prior 8n), and gives an error-detecting 8-T Toffoli
variant (post-selection suppresses error from 4p to 28p^2 to lowest order).

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Toffoli whose target is not a fresh ancilla (in-place targets, e.g.
the final Toffoli of a tof_n ladder, MAJ/UMA steps of a Cuccaro adder) when one clean ancilla is available.
Equivalent to card 01 used as compute + CNOT + uncompute.

**Cost.** 4 T, 1 clean ancilla, 1 measurement, 1 classically controlled CZ per Toffoli (vs 7 T, 0 ancillas).
T-depth can be 1 with the AND written in T-depth-one form (card 04).

**Verification mode: relaxed.** Uses an ancilla precondition and a measurement; check with the
specification contract (invariant 2), not unitary equality.

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`).** Standard Toffoli `ir._CCX`: 7 T, 6 CX,
distance 3e-33 to CCX (`toffoli_7T`). The 4-T AND gadget and its measurement uncompute are verified under
`temporary_and`; the Jones Toffoli is AND -> CX(anc, c) -> uncompute = 4 T (`jones_toffoli`, derived count).
In the suite: every ccz in tof_n / barenco_tof_n / adders is a candidate (MANIFEST.csv `ccx_count`).

**Citation.** C. Jones, "Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate",
*Phys. Rev. A* 87, 022328 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.87.022328, arXiv:1212.5069 (arXiv title: "Novel
constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate").

### 08_pyzx_zx_simplification
# ZX-calculus T-count reduction / phase teleportation (Kissinger & van de Wetering 2020)

**What it does.** Converts the circuit to a ZX-diagram, simplifies it to a graph-like normal form
(local complementation and pivoting remove interior Clifford spiders), gadgetizes phases so non-Clifford
phases on the same parity meet and fuse across Hadamards ("phase teleportation"), then extracts a circuit.
Phase teleportation does not change the number or location of non-phase gates; it also works with arbitrary
and symbolic phases. The same simplifier often proves the optimized circuit equal to the original.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T or Clifford+Rz circuit; strongest where Hadamards split phase
polynomials into regions that phase folding alone cannot merge (Toffoli-heavy arithmetic). It cannot
introduce ancillas or measurements, so it stays at the unitary T-count (e.g. 8n for ripple-carry adders).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count in our runs; no ancillas, no measurements. Extraction can increase CNOT
count (TKET / basic_optimization help).

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving). Self-check: `zx.Circuit.verify_equality`; the project
re-checks every output independently (dense unitary / statevector / sparse basis pairs).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/bench_runs/run2/`, pyzx 0.10.7, full_reduce -> extract_circuit ->
to_basic_gates -> basic_optimization).** tof_3: 21 -> 15 T; adder_8: 399 -> 173 T; cuccaro_4: 56 -> 32 T;
all verified against the input. The paper's Table 1 (arXiv:1903.10477v2 p.4) lists 15 for tof3 and 173 for
adder8 (PyZX column).

**Citation.** A. Kissinger, J. van de Wetering, "Reducing the number of non-Clifford gates in quantum
circuits", *Phys. Rev. A* 102, 022406 (2020), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.102.022406, arXiv:1903.10477 (arXiv title:
"Reducing T-count with the ZX-calculus").

### 07_phase_folding_tpar
# Phase folding and T-par (Amy, Maslov, Mosca 2014)

**What it does.** Inside a {CNOT, X, T, S, Z} region every phase gate applies omega^k to a parity (XOR of
input variables) of the region's inputs: the region is a phase polynomial plus a linear reversible map.
Terms on the same parity merge (T + T = S, T + T^dagger = I), which cuts T-count ("phase folding"); T-par then
re-synthesizes each region, grouping parities into T layers by matroid partitioning to minimize T-depth,
optionally with ancillas. Hadamard gates bound the regions.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T circuit with repeated parities across CNOT networks: expanded
Toffoli cascades (each 7-T Toffoli is 7 parity terms), adders, GF(2^n) multipliers, Hamming / hwb circuits.
Also on Clifford+Rz with arbitrary angles (merge angles on equal parities).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count; no ancillas or measurements for T-count reduction (ancillas only for
T-depth). Reported on its benchmarks: up to 65.7 % T-count and 87.6 % T-depth reduction without ancillae.

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving; D[omega] check of the rewritten window).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`, key `phase_folding_parity`).**
`cx(0,1) t(1) cx(0,1)` and `cx(1,0) t(0) cx(1,0)` both put T on parity x0+x1; the two terms fold into S on
that parity: 2 T -> 0 T (pyzx), dense-unitary distance 1e-16. The project already has a deterministic
phase-folding pass (`circuitevolve/blocks/passes.py`).

**Citation.** M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, "Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits
via matroid partitioning", *IEEE Trans. Comput.-Aided Des. Integr. Circuits Syst.* 33(10), 1476-1489 (2014),
doi:10.1109/TCAD.2014.2341953, arXiv:1303.2042.

### 02_jones_toffoli_measurement
# Toffoli with 4 T via measurement (Jones 2013)

**What it does.** Implements a full Toffoli `ccx(a, b, c)` with Clifford operations plus four T gates
instead of seven: compute `a AND b` into one clean ancilla (4 T), CNOT the ancilla onto `c`, then erase the
ancilla by X-basis measurement and a classically controlled CZ(a, b). Jones also shows that adding n
control inputs to a controlled gate costs 4n T (best prior 8n), and gives an error-detecting 8-T Toffoli
variant (post-selection suppresses error from 4p to 28p^2 to lowest order).

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Toffoli whose target is not a fresh ancilla (in-place targets, e.g.
the final Toffoli of a tof_n ladder, MAJ/UMA steps of a Cuccaro adder) when one clean ancilla is available.
Equivalent to card 01 used as compute + CNOT + uncompute.

**Cost.** 4 T, 1 clean ancilla, 1 measurement, 1 classically controlled CZ per Toffoli (vs 7 T, 0 ancillas).
T-depth can be 1 with the AND written in T-depth-one form (card 04).

**Verification mode: relaxed.** Uses an ancilla precondition and a measurement; check with the
specification contract (invariant 2), not unitary equality.

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`).** Standard Toffoli `ir._CCX`: 7 T, 6 CX,
distance 3e-33 to CCX (`toffoli_7T`). The 4-T AND gadget and its measurement uncompute are verified under
`temporary_and`; the Jones Toffoli is AND -> CX(anc, c) -> uncompute = 4 T (`jones_toffoli`, derived count).
In the suite: every ccz in tof_n / barenco_tof_n / adders is a candidate (MANIFEST.csv `ccx_count`).

**Citation.** C. Jones, "Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate",
*Phys. Rev. A* 87, 022328 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.87.022328, arXiv:1212.5069 (arXiv title: "Novel
constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate").

### 08_pyzx_zx_simplification
# ZX-calculus T-count reduction / phase teleportation (Kissinger & van de Wetering 2020)

**What it does.** Converts the circuit to a ZX-diagram, simplifies it to a graph-like normal form
(local complementation and pivoting remove interior Clifford spiders), gadgetizes phases so non-Clifford
phases on the same parity meet and fuse across Hadamards ("phase teleportation"), then extracts a circuit.
Phase teleportation does not change the number or location of non-phase gates; it also works with arbitrary
and symbolic phases. The same simplifier often proves the optimized circuit equal to the original.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T or Clifford+Rz circuit; strongest where Hadamards split phase
polynomials into regions that phase folding alone cannot merge (Toffoli-heavy arithmetic). It cannot
introduce ancillas or measurements, so it stays at the unitary T-count (e.g. 8n for ripple-carry adders).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count in our runs; no ancillas, no measurements. Extraction can increase CNOT
count (TKET / basic_optimization help).

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving). Self-check: `zx.Circuit.verify_equality`; the project
re-checks every output independently (dense unitary / statevector / sparse basis pairs).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/bench_runs/run2/`, pyzx 0.10.7, full_reduce -> extract_circuit ->
to_basic_gates -> basic_optimization).** tof_3: 21 -> 15 T; adder_8: 399 -> 173 T; cuccaro_4: 56 -> 32 T;
all verified against the input. The paper's Table 1 (arXiv:1903.10477v2 p.4) lists 15 for tof3 and 173 for
adder8 (PyZX column).

**Citation.** A. Kissinger, J. van de Wetering, "Reducing the number of non-Clifford gates in quantum
circuits", *Phys. Rev. A* 102, 022406 (2020), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.102.022406, arXiv:1903.10477 (arXiv title:
"Reducing T-count with the ZX-calculus").

### 07_phase_folding_tpar
# Phase folding and T-par (Amy, Maslov, Mosca 2014)

**What it does.** Inside a {CNOT, X, T, S, Z} region every phase gate applies omega^k to a parity (XOR of
input variables) of the region's inputs: the region is a phase polynomial plus a linear reversible map.
Terms on the same parity merge (T + T = S, T + T^dagger = I), which cuts T-count ("phase folding"); T-par then
re-synthesizes each region, grouping parities into T layers by matroid partitioning to minimize T-depth,
optionally with ancillas. Hadamard gates bound the regions.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T circuit with repeated parities across CNOT networks: expanded
Toffoli cascades (each 7-T Toffoli is 7 parity terms), adders, GF(2^n) multipliers, Hamming / hwb circuits.
Also on Clifford+Rz with arbitrary angles (merge angles on equal parities).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count; no ancillas or measurements for T-count reduction (ancillas only for
T-depth). Reported on its benchmarks: up to 65.7 % T-count and 87.6 % T-depth reduction without ancillae.

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving; D[omega] check of the rewritten window).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`, key `phase_folding_parity`).**
`cx(0,1) t(1) cx(0,1)` and `cx(1,0) t(0) cx(1,0)` both put T on parity x0+x1; the two terms fold into S on
that parity: 2 T -> 0 T (pyzx), dense-unitary distance 1e-16. The project already has a deterministic
phase-folding pass (`circuitevolve/blocks/passes.py`).

**Citation.** M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, "Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits
via matroid partitioning", *IEEE Trans. Comput.-Aided Des. Integr. Circuits Syst.* 33(10), 1476-1489 (2014),
doi:10.1109/TCAD.2014.2341953, arXiv:1303.2042.

### 02_jones_toffoli_measurement
# Toffoli with 4 T via measurement (Jones 2013)

**What it does.** Implements a full Toffoli `ccx(a, b, c)` with Clifford operations plus four T gates
instead of seven: compute `a AND b` into one clean ancilla (4 T), CNOT the ancilla onto `c`, then erase the
ancilla by X-basis measurement and a classically controlled CZ(a, b). Jones also shows that adding n
control inputs to a controlled gate costs 4n T (best prior 8n), and gives an error-detecting 8-T Toffoli
variant (post-selection suppresses error from 4p to 28p^2 to lowest order).

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Toffoli whose target is not a fresh ancilla (in-place targets, e.g.
the final Toffoli of a tof_n ladder, MAJ/UMA steps of a Cuccaro adder) when one clean ancilla is available.
Equivalent to card 01 used as compute + CNOT + uncompute.

**Cost.** 4 T, 1 clean ancilla, 1 measurement, 1 classically controlled CZ per Toffoli (vs 7 T, 0 ancillas).
T-depth can be 1 with the AND written in T-depth-one form (card 04).

**Verification mode: relaxed.** Uses an ancilla precondition and a measurement; check with the
specification contract (invariant 2), not unitary equality.

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`).** Standard Toffoli `ir._CCX`: 7 T, 6 CX,
distance 3e-33 to CCX (`toffoli_7T`). The 4-T AND gadget and its measurement uncompute are verified under
`temporary_and`; the Jones Toffoli is AND -> CX(anc, c) -> uncompute = 4 T (`jones_toffoli`, derived count).
In the suite: every ccz in tof_n / barenco_tof_n / adders is a candidate (MANIFEST.csv `ccx_count`).

**Citation.** C. Jones, "Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate",
*Phys. Rev. A* 87, 022328 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.87.022328, arXiv:1212.5069 (arXiv title: "Novel
constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate").

### 08_pyzx_zx_simplification
# ZX-calculus T-count reduction / phase teleportation (Kissinger & van de Wetering 2020)

**What it does.** Converts the circuit to a ZX-diagram, simplifies it to a graph-like normal form
(local complementation and pivoting remove interior Clifford spiders), gadgetizes phases so non-Clifford
phases on the same parity meet and fuse across Hadamards ("phase teleportation"), then extracts a circuit.
Phase teleportation does not change the number or location of non-phase gates; it also works with arbitrary
and symbolic phases. The same simplifier often proves the optimized circuit equal to the original.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T or Clifford+Rz circuit; strongest where Hadamards split phase
polynomials into regions that phase folding alone cannot merge (Toffoli-heavy arithmetic). It cannot
introduce ancillas or measurements, so it stays at the unitary T-count (e.g. 8n for ripple-carry adders).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count in our runs; no ancillas, no measurements. Extraction can increase CNOT
count (TKET / basic_optimization help).

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving). Self-check: `zx.Circuit.verify_equality`; the project
re-checks every output independently (dense unitary / statevector / sparse basis pairs).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/bench_runs/run2/`, pyzx 0.10.7, full_reduce -> extract_circuit ->
to_basic_gates -> basic_optimization).** tof_3: 21 -> 15 T; adder_8: 399 -> 173 T; cuccaro_4: 56 -> 32 T;
all verified against the input. The paper's Table 1 (arXiv:1903.10477v2 p.4) lists 15 for tof3 and 173 for
adder8 (PyZX column).

**Citation.** A. Kissinger, J. van de Wetering, "Reducing the number of non-Clifford gates in quantum
circuits", *Phys. Rev. A* 102, 022406 (2020), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.102.022406, arXiv:1903.10477 (arXiv title:
"Reducing T-count with the ZX-calculus").

### 07_phase_folding_tpar
# Phase folding and T-par (Amy, Maslov, Mosca 2014)

**What it does.** Inside a {CNOT, X, T, S, Z} region every phase gate applies omega^k to a parity (XOR of
input variables) of the region's inputs: the region is a phase polynomial plus a linear reversible map.
Terms on the same parity merge (T + T = S, T + T^dagger = I), which cuts T-count ("phase folding"); T-par then
re-synthesizes each region, grouping parities into T layers by matroid partitioning to minimize T-depth,
optionally with ancillas. Hadamard gates bound the regions.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T circuit with repeated parities across CNOT networks: expanded
Toffoli cascades (each 7-T Toffoli is 7 parity terms), adders, GF(2^n) multipliers, Hamming / hwb circuits.
Also on Clifford+Rz with arbitrary angles (merge angles on equal parities).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count; no ancillas or measurements for T-count reduction (ancillas only for
T-depth). Reported on its benchmarks: up to 65.7 % T-count and 87.6 % T-depth reduction without ancillae.

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving; D[omega] check of the rewritten window).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`, key `phase_folding_parity`).**
`cx(0,1) t(1) cx(0,1)` and `cx(1,0) t(0) cx(1,0)` both put T on parity x0+x1; the two terms fold into S on
that parity: 2 T -> 0 T (pyzx), dense-unitary distance 1e-16. The project already has a deterministic
phase-folding pass (`circuitevolve/blocks/passes.py`).

**Citation.** M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, "Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits
via matroid partitioning", *IEEE Trans. Comput.-Aided Des. Integr. Circuits Syst.* 33(10), 1476-1489 (2014),
doi:10.1109/TCAD.2014.2341953, arXiv:1303.2042.

Equivalent to card 01 used as compute + CNOT + uncompute.

**Cost.** 4 T, 1 clean ancilla, 1 measurement, 1 classically controlled CZ per Toffoli (vs 7 T, 0 ancillas).
T-depth can be 1 with the AND written in T-depth-one form (card 04).

**Verification mode: relaxed.** Uses an ancilla precondition and a measurement; check with the
specification contract (invariant 2), not unitary equality.

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`).** Standard Toffoli `ir._CCX`: 7 T, 6 CX,
distance 3e-33 to CCX (`toffoli_7T`). The 4-T AND gadget and its measurement uncompute are verified under
`temporary_and`; the Jones Toffoli is AND -> CX(anc, c) -> uncompute = 4 T (`jones_toffoli`, derived count).
In the suite: every ccz in tof_n / barenco_tof_n / adders is a candidate (MANIFEST.csv `ccx_count`).

*Phys. Rev. A* 87, 022328 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.87.022328, arXiv:1212.5069 (arXiv title: "Novel
constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate").

### 08_pyzx_zx_simplification
# ZX-calculus T-count reduction / phase teleportation (Kissinger & van de Wetering 2020)

**What it does.** Converts the circuit to a ZX-diagram, simplifies it to a graph-like normal form
(local complementation and pivoting remove interior Clifford spiders), gadgetizes phases so non-Clifford
phases on the same parity meet and fuse across Hadamards ("phase teleportation"), then extracts a circuit.
Phase teleportation does not change the number or location of non-phase gates; it also works with arbitrary
and symbolic phases. The same simplifier often proves the optimized circuit equal to the original.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T or Clifford+Rz circuit; strongest where Hadamards split phase
polynomials into regions that phase folding alone cannot merge (Toffoli-heavy arithmetic). It cannot
introduce ancillas or measurements, so it stays at the unitary T-count (e.g. 8n for ripple-carry adders).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count in our runs; no ancillas, no measurements. Extraction can increase CNOT
count (TKET / basic_optimization help).

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving). Self-check: `zx.Circuit.verify_equality`; the project
re-checks every output independently (dense unitary / statevector / sparse basis pairs).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/bench_runs/run2/`, pyzx 0.10.7, full_reduce -> extract_circuit ->
to_basic_gates -> basic_optimization).** tof_3: 21 -> 15 T; adder_8: 399 -> 173 T; cuccaro_4: 56 -> 32 T;
all verified against the input. The paper's Table 1 (arXiv:1903.10477v2 p.4) lists 15 for tof3 and 173 for
adder8 (PyZX column).

**Citation.** A. Kissinger, J. van de Wetering, "Reducing the number of non-Clifford gates in quantum
circuits", *Phys. Rev. A* 102, 022406 (2020), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.102.022406, arXiv:1903.10477 (arXiv title:
"Reducing T-count with the ZX-calculus").

### 07_phase_folding_tpar
# Phase folding and T-par (Amy, Maslov, Mosca 2014)

**What it does.** Inside a {CNOT, X, T, S, Z} region every phase gate applies omega^k to a parity (XOR of
input variables) of the region's inputs: the region is a phase polynomial plus a linear reversible map.
Terms on the same parity merge (T + T = S, T + T^dagger = I), which cuts T-count ("phase folding"); T-par then
re-synthesizes each region, grouping parities into T layers by matroid partitioning to minimize T-depth,
optionally with ancillas. Hadamard gates bound the regions.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T circuit with repeated parities across CNOT networks: expanded
Toffoli cascades (each 7-T Toffoli is 7 parity terms), adders, GF(2^n) multipliers, Hamming / hwb circuits.
Also on Clifford+Rz with arbitrary angles (merge angles on equal parities).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count; no ancillas or measurements for T-count reduction (ancillas only for
T-depth). Reported on its benchmarks: up to 65.7 % T-count and 87.6 % T-depth reduction without ancillae.

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving; D[omega] check of the rewritten window).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`, key `phase_folding_parity`).**
`cx(0,1) t(1) cx(0,1)` and `cx(1,0) t(0) cx(1,0)` both put T on parity x0+x1; the two terms fold into S on
that parity: 2 T -> 0 T (pyzx), dense-unitary distance 1e-16. The project already has a deterministic
phase-folding pass (`circuitevolve/blocks/passes.py`).

**Citation.** M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, "Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits
via matroid partitioning", *IEEE Trans. Comput.-Aided Des. Integr. Circuits Syst.* 33(10), 1476-1489 (2014),
doi:10.1109/TCAD.2014.2341953, arXiv:1303.2042.

### 02_jones_toffoli_measurement
# Toffoli with 4 T via measurement (Jones 2013)

**What it does.** Implements a full Toffoli `ccx(a, b, c)` with Clifford operations plus four T gates
instead of seven: compute `a AND b` into one clean ancilla (4 T), CNOT the ancilla onto `c`, then erase the
ancilla by X-basis measurement and a classically controlled CZ(a, b). Jones also shows that adding n
control inputs to a controlled gate costs 4n T (best prior 8n), and gives an error-detecting 8-T Toffoli
variant (post-selection suppresses error from 4p to 28p^2 to lowest order).

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Toffoli whose target is not a fresh ancilla (in-place targets, e.g.
the final Toffoli of a tof_n ladder, MAJ/UMA steps of a Cuccaro adder) when one clean ancilla is available.
Equivalent to card 01 used as compute + CNOT + uncompute.

**Cost.** 4 T, 1 clean ancilla, 1 measurement, 1 classically controlled CZ per Toffoli (vs 7 T, 0 ancillas).
T-depth can be 1 with the AND written in T-depth-one form (card 04).

**Verification mode: relaxed.** Uses an ancilla precondition and a measurement; check with the
specification contract (invariant 2), not unitary equality.

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`).** Standard Toffoli `ir._CCX`: 7 T, 6 CX,
distance 3e-33 to CCX (`toffoli_7T`). The 4-T AND gadget and its measurement uncompute are verified under
`temporary_and`; the Jones Toffoli is AND -> CX(anc, c) -> uncompute = 4 T (`jones_toffoli`, derived count).
In the suite: every ccz in tof_n / barenco_tof_n / adders is a candidate (MANIFEST.csv `ccx_count`).

**Citation.** C. Jones, "Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate",
*Phys. Rev. A* 87, 022328 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.87.022328, arXiv:1212.5069 (arXiv title: "Novel
constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate").

### 08_pyzx_zx_simplification
# ZX-calculus T-count reduction / phase teleportation (Kissinger & van de Wetering 2020)

**What it does.** Converts the circuit to a ZX-diagram, simplifies it to a graph-like normal form
(local complementation and pivoting remove interior Clifford spiders), gadgetizes phases so non-Clifford
phases on the same parity meet and fuse across Hadamards ("phase teleportation"), then extracts a circuit.
Phase teleportation does not change the number or location of non-phase gates; it also works with arbitrary
and symbolic phases. The same simplifier often proves the optimized circuit equal to the original.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T or Clifford+Rz circuit; strongest where Hadamards split phase
polynomials into regions that phase folding alone cannot merge (Toffoli-heavy arithmetic). It cannot
introduce ancillas or measurements, so it stays at the unitary T-count (e.g. 8n for ripple-carry adders).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count in our runs; no ancillas, no measurements. Extraction can increase CNOT
count (TKET / basic_optimization help).

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving). Self-check: `zx.Circuit.verify_equality`; the project
re-checks every output independently (dense unitary / statevector / sparse basis pairs).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/bench_runs/run2/`, pyzx 0.10.7, full_reduce -> extract_circuit ->
to_basic_gates -> basic_optimization).** tof_3: 21 -> 15 T; adder_8: 399 -> 173 T; cuccaro_4: 56 -> 32 T;
all verified against the input. The paper's Table 1 (arXiv:1903.10477v2 p.4) lists 15 for tof3 and 173 for
adder8 (PyZX column).

**Citation.** A. Kissinger, J. van de Wetering, "Reducing the number of non-Clifford gates in quantum
circuits", *Phys. Rev. A* 102, 022406 (2020), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.102.022406, arXiv:1903.10477 (arXiv title:
"Reducing T-count with the ZX-calculus").

### 07_phase_folding_tpar
# Phase folding and T-par (Amy, Maslov, Mosca 2014)

**What it does.** Inside a {CNOT, X, T, S, Z} region every phase gate applies omega^k to a parity (XOR of
input variables) of the region's inputs: the region is a phase polynomial plus a linear reversible map.
Terms on the same parity merge (T + T = S, T + T^dagger = I), which cuts T-count ("phase folding"); T-par then
re-synthesizes each region, grouping parities into T layers by matroid partitioning to minimize T-depth,
optionally with ancillas. Hadamard gates bound the regions.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T circuit with repeated parities across CNOT networks: expanded
Toffoli cascades (each 7-T Toffoli is 7 parity terms), adders, GF(2^n) multipliers, Hamming / hwb circuits.
Also on Clifford+Rz with arbitrary angles (merge angles on equal parities).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count; no ancillas or measurements for T-count reduction (ancillas only for
T-depth). Reported on its benchmarks: up to 65.7 % T-count and 87.6 % T-depth reduction without ancillae.

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving; D[omega] check of the rewritten window).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`, key `phase_folding_parity`).**
`cx(0,1) t(1) cx(0,1)` and `cx(1,0) t(0) cx(1,0)` both put T on parity x0+x1; the two terms fold into S on
that parity: 2 T -> 0 T (pyzx), dense-unitary distance 1e-16. The project already has a deterministic
phase-folding pass (`circuitevolve/blocks/passes.py`).

**Citation.** M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, "Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits
via matroid partitioning", *IEEE Trans. Comput.-Aided Des. Integr. Circuits Syst.* 33(10), 1476-1489 (2014),
doi:10.1109/TCAD.2014.2341953, arXiv:1303.2042.

### 02_jones_toffoli_measurement
# Toffoli with 4 T via measurement (Jones 2013)

**What it does.** Implements a full Toffoli `ccx(a, b, c)` with Clifford operations plus four T gates
instead of seven: compute `a AND b` into one clean ancilla (4 T), CNOT the ancilla onto `c`, then erase the
ancilla by X-basis measurement and a classically controlled CZ(a, b). Jones also shows that adding n
control inputs to a controlled gate costs 4n T (best prior 8n), and gives an error-detecting 8-T Toffoli
variant (post-selection suppresses error from 4p to 28p^2 to lowest order).

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Toffoli whose target is not a fresh ancilla (in-place targets, e.g.
the final Toffoli of a tof_n ladder, MAJ/UMA steps of a Cuccaro adder) when one clean ancilla is available.
Equivalent to card 01 used as compute + CNOT + uncompute.

**Cost.** 4 T, 1 clean ancilla, 1 measurement, 1 classically controlled CZ per Toffoli (vs 7 T, 0 ancillas).
T-depth can be 1 with the AND written in T-depth-one form (card 04).

**Verification mode: relaxed.** Uses an ancilla precondition and a measurement; check with the
specification contract (invariant 2), not unitary equality.

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`).** Standard Toffoli `ir._CCX`: 7 T, 6 CX,
distance 3e-33 to CCX (`toffoli_7T`). The 4-T AND gadget and its measurement uncompute are verified under
`temporary_and`; the Jones Toffoli is AND -> CX(anc, c) -> uncompute = 4 T (`jones_toffoli`, derived count).
In the suite: every ccz in tof_n / barenco_tof_n / adders is a candidate (MANIFEST.csv `ccx_count`).

**Citation.** C. Jones, "Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate",
*Phys. Rev. A* 87, 022328 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.87.022328, arXiv:1212.5069 (arXiv title: "Novel
constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate").

### 02_jones_toffoli_measurement
# Toffoli with 4 T via measurement (Jones 2013)

**What it does.** Implements a full Toffoli `ccx(a, b, c)` with Clifford operations plus four T gates
instead of seven: compute `a AND b` into one clean ancilla (4 T), CNOT the ancilla onto `c`, then erase the
ancilla by X-basis measurement and a classically controlled CZ(a, b). Jones also shows that adding n
control inputs to a controlled gate costs 4n T (best prior 8n), and gives an error-detecting 8-T Toffoli
variant (post-selection suppresses error from 4p to 28p^2 to lowest order).

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Toffoli whose target is not a fresh ancilla (in-place targets, e.g.
the final Toffoli of a tof_n ladder, MAJ/UMA steps of a Cuccaro adder) when one clean ancilla is available.
Equivalent to card 01 used as compute + CNOT + uncompute.

**Cost.** 4 T, 1 clean ancilla, 1 measurement, 1 classically controlled CZ per Toffoli (vs 7 T, 0 ancillas).
T-depth can be 1 with the AND written in T-depth-one form (card 04).

**Verification mode: relaxed.** Uses an ancilla precondition and a measurement; check with the
specification contract (invariant 2), not unitary equality.

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`).** Standard Toffoli `ir._CCX`: 7 T, 6 CX,
distance 3e-33 to CCX (`toffoli_7T`). The 4-T AND gadget and its measurement uncompute are verified under
`temporary_and`; the Jones Toffoli is AND -> CX(anc, c) -> uncompute = 4 T (`jones_toffoli`, derived count).
In the suite: every ccz in tof_n / barenco_tof_n / adders is a candidate (MANIFEST.csv `ccx_count`).

**Citation.** C. Jones, "Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate",
*Phys. Rev. A* 87, 022328 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.87.022328, arXiv:1212.5069 (arXiv title: "Novel
constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate").

### 08_pyzx_zx_simplification
# ZX-calculus T-count reduction / phase teleportation (Kissinger & van de Wetering 2020)

**What it does.** Converts the circuit to a ZX-diagram, simplifies it to a graph-like normal form
(local complementation and pivoting remove interior Clifford spiders), gadgetizes phases so non-Clifford
phases on the same parity meet and fuse across Hadamards ("phase teleportation"), then extracts a circuit.
Phase teleportation does not change the number or location of non-phase gates; it also works with arbitrary
and symbolic phases. The same simplifier often proves the optimized circuit equal to the original.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T or Clifford+Rz circuit; strongest where Hadamards split phase
polynomials into regions that phase folding alone cannot merge (Toffoli-heavy arithmetic). It cannot
introduce ancillas or measurements, so it stays at the unitary T-count (e.g. 8n for ripple-carry adders).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count in our runs; no ancillas, no measurements. Extraction can increase CNOT
count (TKET / basic_optimization help).

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving). Self-check: `zx.Circuit.verify_equality`; the project
re-checks every output independently (dense unitary / statevector / sparse basis pairs).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/bench_runs/run2/`, pyzx 0.10.7, full_reduce -> extract_circuit ->
to_basic_gates -> basic_optimization).** tof_3: 21 -> 15 T; adder_8: 399 -> 173 T; cuccaro_4: 56 -> 32 T;
all verified against the input. The paper's Table 1 (arXiv:1903.10477v2 p.4) lists 15 for tof3 and 173 for
adder8 (PyZX column).

**Citation.** A. Kissinger, J. van de Wetering, "Reducing the number of non-Clifford gates in quantum
circuits", *Phys. Rev. A* 102, 022406 (2020), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.102.022406, arXiv:1903.10477 (arXiv title:
"Reducing T-count with the ZX-calculus").

### 07_phase_folding_tpar
# Phase folding and T-par (Amy, Maslov, Mosca 2014)

**What it does.** Inside a {CNOT, X, T, S, Z} region every phase gate applies omega^k to a parity (XOR of
input variables) of the region's inputs: the region is a phase polynomial plus a linear reversible map.
Terms on the same parity merge (T + T = S, T + T^dagger = I), which cuts T-count ("phase folding"); T-par then
re-synthesizes each region, grouping parities into T layers by matroid partitioning to minimize T-depth,
optionally with ancillas. Hadamard gates bound the regions.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T circuit with repeated parities across CNOT networks: expanded
Toffoli cascades (each 7-T Toffoli is 7 parity terms), adders, GF(2^n) multipliers, Hamming / hwb circuits.
Also on Clifford+Rz with arbitrary angles (merge angles on equal parities).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count; no ancillas or measurements for T-count reduction (ancillas only for
T-depth). Reported on its benchmarks: up to 65.7 % T-count and 87.6 % T-depth reduction without ancillae.

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving; D[omega] check of the rewritten window).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`, key `phase_folding_parity`).**
`cx(0,1) t(1) cx(0,1)` and `cx(1,0) t(0) cx(1,0)` both put T on parity x0+x1; the two terms fold into S on
that parity: 2 T -> 0 T (pyzx), dense-unitary distance 1e-16. The project already has a deterministic
phase-folding pass (`circuitevolve/blocks/passes.py`).

**Citation.** M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, "Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits
via matroid partitioning", *IEEE Trans. Comput.-Aided Des. Integr. Circuits Syst.* 33(10), 1476-1489 (2014),
doi:10.1109/TCAD.2014.2341953, arXiv:1303.2042.

### 02_jones_toffoli_measurement
# Toffoli with 4 T via measurement (Jones 2013)

**What it does.** Implements a full Toffoli `ccx(a, b, c)` with Clifford operations plus four T gates
instead of seven: compute `a AND b` into one clean ancilla (4 T), CNOT the ancilla onto `c`, then erase the
ancilla by X-basis measurement and a classically controlled CZ(a, b). Jones also shows that adding n
control inputs to a controlled gate costs 4n T (best prior 8n), and gives an error-detecting 8-T Toffoli
variant (post-selection suppresses error from 4p to 28p^2 to lowest order).

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Toffoli whose target is not a fresh ancilla (in-place targets, e.g.
the final Toffoli of a tof_n ladder, MAJ/UMA steps of a Cuccaro adder) when one clean ancilla is available.
Equivalent to card 01 used as compute + CNOT + uncompute.

**Cost.** 4 T, 1 clean ancilla, 1 measurement, 1 classically controlled CZ per Toffoli (vs 7 T, 0 ancillas).
T-depth can be 1 with the AND written in T-depth-one form (card 04).

**Verification mode: relaxed.** Uses an ancilla precondition and a measurement; check with the
specification contract (invariant 2), not unitary equality.

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`).** Standard Toffoli `ir._CCX`: 7 T, 6 CX,
distance 3e-33 to CCX (`toffoli_7T`). The 4-T AND gadget and its measurement uncompute are verified under
`temporary_and`; the Jones Toffoli is AND -> CX(anc, c) -> uncompute = 4 T (`jones_toffoli`, derived count).
In the suite: every ccz in tof_n / barenco_tof_n / adders is a candidate (MANIFEST.csv `ccx_count`).

**Citation.** C. Jones, "Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate",
*Phys. Rev. A* 87, 022328 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.87.022328, arXiv:1212.5069 (arXiv title: "Novel
constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate").

### 08_pyzx_zx_simplification
# ZX-calculus T-count reduction / phase teleportation (Kissinger & van de Wetering 2020)

**What it does.** Converts the circuit to a ZX-diagram, simplifies it to a graph-like normal form
(local complementation and pivoting remove interior Clifford spiders), gadgetizes phases so non-Clifford
phases on the same parity meet and fuse across Hadamards ("phase teleportation"), then extracts a circuit.
Phase teleportation does not change the number or location of non-phase gates; it also works with arbitrary
and symbolic phases. The same simplifier often proves the optimized circuit equal to the original.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T or Clifford+Rz circuit; strongest where Hadamards split phase
polynomials into regions that phase folding alone cannot merge (Toffoli-heavy arithmetic). It cannot
introduce ancillas or measurements, so it stays at the unitary T-count (e.g. 8n for ripple-carry adders).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count in our runs; no ancillas, no measurements. Extraction can increase CNOT
count (TKET / basic_optimization help).

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving). Self-check: `zx.Circuit.verify_equality`; the project
re-checks every output independently (dense unitary / statevector / sparse basis pairs).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/bench_runs/run2/`, pyzx 0.10.7, full_reduce -> extract_circuit ->
to_basic_gates -> basic_optimization).** tof_3: 21 -> 15 T; adder_8: 399 -> 173 T; cuccaro_4: 56 -> 32 T;
all verified against the input. The paper's Table 1 (arXiv:1903.10477v2 p.4) lists 15 for tof3 and 173 for
adder8 (PyZX column).

**Citation.** A. Kissinger, J. van de Wetering, "Reducing the number of non-Clifford gates in quantum
circuits", *Phys. Rev. A* 102, 022406 (2020), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.102.022406, arXiv:1903.10477 (arXiv title:
"Reducing T-count with the ZX-calculus").

### 07_phase_folding_tpar
# Phase folding and T-par (Amy, Maslov, Mosca 2014)

**What it does.** Inside a {CNOT, X, T, S, Z} region every phase gate applies omega^k to a parity (XOR of
input variables) of the region's inputs: the region is a phase polynomial plus a linear reversible map.
Terms on the same parity merge (T + T = S, T + T^dagger = I), which cuts T-count ("phase folding"); T-par then
re-synthesizes each region, grouping parities into T layers by matroid partitioning to minimize T-depth,
optionally with ancillas. Hadamard gates bound the regions.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T circuit with repeated parities across CNOT networks: expanded
Toffoli cascades (each 7-T Toffoli is 7 parity terms), adders, GF(2^n) multipliers, Hamming / hwb circuits.
Also on Clifford+Rz with arbitrary angles (merge angles on equal parities).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count; no ancillas or measurements for T-count reduction (ancillas only for
T-depth). Reported on its benchmarks: up to 65.7 % T-count and 87.6 % T-depth reduction without ancillae.

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving; D[omega] check of the rewritten window).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`, key `phase_folding_parity`).**
`cx(0,1) t(1) cx(0,1)` and `cx(1,0) t(0) cx(1,0)` both put T on parity x0+x1; the two terms fold into S on
that parity: 2 T -> 0 T (pyzx), dense-unitary distance 1e-16. The project already has a deterministic
phase-folding pass (`circuitevolve/blocks/passes.py`).

**Citation.** M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, "Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits
via matroid partitioning", *IEEE Trans. Comput.-Aided Des. Integr. Circuits Syst.* 33(10), 1476-1489 (2014),
doi:10.1109/TCAD.2014.2341953, arXiv:1303.2042.

### 02_jones_toffoli_measurement
# Toffoli with 4 T via measurement (Jones 2013)

**What it does.** Implements a full Toffoli `ccx(a, b, c)` with Clifford operations plus four T gates
instead of seven: compute `a AND b` into one clean ancilla (4 T), CNOT the ancilla onto `c`, then erase the
ancilla by X-basis measurement and a classically controlled CZ(a, b). Jones also shows that adding n
control inputs to a controlled gate costs 4n T (best prior 8n), and gives an error-detecting 8-T Toffoli
variant (post-selection suppresses error from 4p to 28p^2 to lowest order).

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Toffoli whose target is not a fresh ancilla (in-place targets, e.g.
the final Toffoli of a tof_n ladder, MAJ/UMA steps of a Cuccaro adder) when one clean ancilla is available.
Equivalent to card 01 used as compute + CNOT + uncompute.

**Cost.** 4 T, 1 clean ancilla, 1 measurement, 1 classically controlled CZ per Toffoli (vs 7 T, 0 ancillas).
T-depth can be 1 with the AND written in T-depth-one form (card 04).

**Verification mode: relaxed.** Uses an ancilla precondition and a measurement; check with the
specification contract (invariant 2), not unitary equality.

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`).** Standard Toffoli `ir._CCX`: 7 T, 6 CX,
distance 3e-33 to CCX (`toffoli_7T`). The 4-T AND gadget and its measurement uncompute are verified under
`temporary_and`; the Jones Toffoli is AND -> CX(anc, c) -> uncompute = 4 T (`jones_toffoli`, derived count).
In the suite: every ccz in tof_n / barenco_tof_n / adders is a candidate (MANIFEST.csv `ccx_count`).

**Citation.** C. Jones, "Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate",
*Phys. Rev. A* 87, 022328 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.87.022328, arXiv:1212.5069 (arXiv title: "Novel
constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate").

### 08_pyzx_zx_simplification
# ZX-calculus T-count reduction / phase teleportation (Kissinger & van de Wetering 2020)

**What it does.** Converts the circuit to a ZX-diagram, simplifies it to a graph-like normal form
(local complementation and pivoting remove interior Clifford spiders), gadgetizes phases so non-Clifford
phases on the same parity meet and fuse across Hadamards ("phase teleportation"), then extracts a circuit.
Phase teleportation does not change the number or location of non-phase gates; it also works with arbitrary
and symbolic phases. The same simplifier often proves the optimized circuit equal to the original.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T or Clifford+Rz circuit; strongest where Hadamards split phase
polynomials into regions that phase folding alone cannot merge (Toffoli-heavy arithmetic). It cannot
introduce ancillas or measurements, so it stays at the unitary T-count (e.g. 8n for ripple-carry adders).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count in our runs; no ancillas, no measurements. Extraction can increase CNOT
count (TKET / basic_optimization help).

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving). Self-check: `zx.Circuit.verify_equality`; the project
re-checks every output independently (dense unitary / statevector / sparse basis pairs).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/bench_runs/run2/`, pyzx 0.10.7, full_reduce -> extract_circuit ->
to_basic_gates -> basic_optimization).** tof_3: 21 -> 15 T; adder_8: 399 -> 173 T; cuccaro_4: 56 -> 32 T;
all verified against the input. The paper's Table 1 (arXiv:1903.10477v2 p.4) lists 15 for tof3 and 173 for
adder8 (PyZX column).

**Citation.** A. Kissinger, J. van de Wetering, "Reducing the number of non-Clifford gates in quantum
circuits", *Phys. Rev. A* 102, 022406 (2020), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.102.022406, arXiv:1903.10477 (arXiv title:
"Reducing T-count with the ZX-calculus").

### 07_phase_folding_tpar
# Phase folding and T-par (Amy, Maslov, Mosca 2014)

**What it does.** Inside a {CNOT, X, T, S, Z} region every phase gate applies omega^k to a parity (XOR of
input variables) of the region's inputs: the region is a phase polynomial plus a linear reversible map.
Terms on the same parity merge (T + T = S, T + T^dagger = I), which cuts T-count ("phase folding"); T-par then
re-synthesizes each region, grouping parities into T layers by matroid partitioning to minimize T-depth,
optionally with ancillas. Hadamard gates bound the regions.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T circuit with repeated parities across CNOT networks: expanded
Toffoli cascades (each 7-T Toffoli is 7 parity terms), adders, GF(2^n) multipliers, Hamming / hwb circuits.
Also on Clifford+Rz with arbitrary angles (merge angles on equal parities).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count; no ancillas or measurements for T-count reduction (ancillas only for
T-depth). Reported on its benchmarks: up to 65.7 % T-count and 87.6 % T-depth reduction without ancillae.

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving; D[omega] check of the rewritten window).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`, key `phase_folding_parity`).**
`cx(0,1) t(1) cx(0,1)` and `cx(1,0) t(0) cx(1,0)` both put T on parity x0+x1; the two terms fold into S on
that parity: 2 T -> 0 T (pyzx), dense-unitary distance 1e-16. The project already has a deterministic
phase-folding pass (`circuitevolve/blocks/passes.py`).

**Citation.** M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, "Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits
via matroid partitioning", *IEEE Trans. Comput.-Aided Des. Integr. Circuits Syst.* 33(10), 1476-1489 (2014),
doi:10.1109/TCAD.2014.2341953, arXiv:1303.2042.

### 02_jones_toffoli_measurement
# Toffoli with 4 T via measurement (Jones 2013)

**What it does.** Implements a full Toffoli `ccx(a, b, c)` with Clifford operations plus four T gates
instead of seven: compute `a AND b` into one clean ancilla (4 T), CNOT the ancilla onto `c`, then erase the
ancilla by X-basis measurement and a classically controlled CZ(a, b). Jones also shows that adding n
control inputs to a controlled gate costs 4n T (best prior 8n), and gives an error-detecting 8-T Toffoli
variant (post-selection suppresses error from 4p to 28p^2 to lowest order).

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Toffoli whose target is not a fresh ancilla (in-place targets, e.g.
the final Toffoli of a tof_n ladder, MAJ/UMA steps of a Cuccaro adder) when one clean ancilla is available.
Equivalent to card 01 used as compute + CNOT + uncompute.

**Cost.** 4 T, 1 clean ancilla, 1 measurement, 1 classically controlled CZ per Toffoli (vs 7 T, 0 ancillas).
T-depth can be 1 with the AND written in T-depth-one form (card 04).

**Verification mode: relaxed.** Uses an ancilla precondition and a measurement; check with the
specification contract (invariant 2), not unitary equality.

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`).** Standard Toffoli `ir._CCX`: 7 T, 6 CX,
distance 3e-33 to CCX (`toffoli_7T`). The 4-T AND gadget and its measurement uncompute are verified under
`temporary_and`; the Jones Toffoli is AND -> CX(anc, c) -> uncompute = 4 T (`jones_toffoli`, derived count).
In the suite: every ccz in tof_n / barenco_tof_n / adders is a candidate (MANIFEST.csv `ccx_count`).

**Citation.** C. Jones, "Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate",
*Phys. Rev. A* 87, 022328 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.87.022328, arXiv:1212.5069 (arXiv title: "Novel
constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate").

### 08_pyzx_zx_simplification
# ZX-calculus T-count reduction / phase teleportation (Kissinger & van de Wetering 2020)

**What it does.** Converts the circuit to a ZX-diagram, simplifies it to a graph-like normal form
(local complementation and pivoting remove interior Clifford spiders), gadgetizes phases so non-Clifford
phases on the same parity meet and fuse across Hadamards ("phase teleportation"), then extracts a circuit.
Phase teleportation does not change the number or location of non-phase gates; it also works with arbitrary
and symbolic phases. The same simplifier often proves the optimized circuit equal to the original.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T or Clifford+Rz circuit; strongest where Hadamards split phase
polynomials into regions that phase folding alone cannot merge (Toffoli-heavy arithmetic). It cannot
introduce ancillas or measurements, so it stays at the unitary T-count (e.g. 8n for ripple-carry adders).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count in our runs; no ancillas, no measurements. Extraction can increase CNOT
count (TKET / basic_optimization help).

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving). Self-check: `zx.Circuit.verify_equality`; the project
re-checks every output independently (dense unitary / statevector / sparse basis pairs).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/bench_runs/run2/`, pyzx 0.10.7, full_reduce -> extract_circuit ->
to_basic_gates -> basic_optimization).** tof_3: 21 -> 15 T; adder_8: 399 -> 173 T; cuccaro_4: 56 -> 32 T;
all verified against the input. The paper's Table 1 (arXiv:1903.10477v2 p.4) lists 15 for tof3 and 173 for
adder8 (PyZX column).

**Citation.** A. Kissinger, J. van de Wetering, "Reducing the number of non-Clifford gates in quantum
circuits", *Phys. Rev. A* 102, 022406 (2020), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.102.022406, arXiv:1903.10477 (arXiv title:
"Reducing T-count with the ZX-calculus").

### 07_phase_folding_tpar
# Phase folding and T-par (Amy, Maslov, Mosca 2014)

**What it does.** Inside a {CNOT, X, T, S, Z} region every phase gate applies omega^k to a parity (XOR of
input variables) of the region's inputs: the region is a phase polynomial plus a linear reversible map.
Terms on the same parity merge (T + T = S, T + T^dagger = I), which cuts T-count ("phase folding"); T-par then
re-synthesizes each region, grouping parities into T layers by matroid partitioning to minimize T-depth,
optionally with ancillas. Hadamard gates bound the regions.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T circuit with repeated parities across CNOT networks: expanded
Toffoli cascades (each 7-T Toffoli is 7 parity terms), adders, GF(2^n) multipliers, Hamming / hwb circuits.
Also on Clifford+Rz with arbitrary angles (merge angles on equal parities).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count; no ancillas or measurements for T-count reduction (ancillas only for
T-depth). Reported on its benchmarks: up to 65.7 % T-count and 87.6 % T-depth reduction without ancillae.

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving; D[omega] check of the rewritten window).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`, key `phase_folding_parity`).**
`cx(0,1) t(1) cx(0,1)` and `cx(1,0) t(0) cx(1,0)` both put T on parity x0+x1; the two terms fold into S on
that parity: 2 T -> 0 T (pyzx), dense-unitary distance 1e-16. The project already has a deterministic
phase-folding pass (`circuitevolve/blocks/passes.py`).

**Citation.** M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, "Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits
via matroid partitioning", *IEEE Trans. Comput.-Aided Des. Integr. Circuits Syst.* 33(10), 1476-1489 (2014),
doi:10.1109/TCAD.2014.2341953, arXiv:1303.2042.

### 02_jones_toffoli_measurement
# Toffoli with 4 T via measurement (Jones 2013)

**What it does.** Implements a full Toffoli `ccx(a, b, c)` with Clifford operations plus four T gates
instead of seven: compute `a AND b` into one clean ancilla (4 T), CNOT the ancilla onto `c`, then erase the
ancilla by X-basis measurement and a classically controlled CZ(a, b). Jones also shows that adding n
control inputs to a controlled gate costs 4n T (best prior 8n), and gives an error-detecting 8-T Toffoli
variant (post-selection suppresses error from 4p to 28p^2 to lowest order).

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Toffoli whose target is not a fresh ancilla (in-place targets, e.g.
the final Toffoli of a tof_n ladder, MAJ/UMA steps of a Cuccaro adder) when one clean ancilla is available.
Equivalent to card 01 used as compute + CNOT + uncompute.

**Cost.** 4 T, 1 clean ancilla, 1 measurement, 1 classically controlled CZ per Toffoli (vs 7 T, 0 ancillas).
T-depth can be 1 with the AND written in T-depth-one form (card 04).

**Verification mode: relaxed.** Uses an ancilla precondition and a measurement; check with the
specification contract (invariant 2), not unitary equality.

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`).** Standard Toffoli `ir._CCX`: 7 T, 6 CX,
distance 3e-33 to CCX (`toffoli_7T`). The 4-T AND gadget and its measurement uncompute are verified under
`temporary_and`; the Jones Toffoli is AND -> CX(anc, c) -> uncompute = 4 T (`jones_toffoli`, derived count).
In the suite: every ccz in tof_n / barenco_tof_n / adders is a candidate (MANIFEST.csv `ccx_count`).

**Citation.** C. Jones, "Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate",
*Phys. Rev. A* 87, 022328 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.87.022328, arXiv:1212.5069 (arXiv title: "Novel
constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate").

### 08_pyzx_zx_simplification
# ZX-calculus T-count reduction / phase teleportation (Kissinger & van de Wetering 2020)

**What it does.** Converts the circuit to a ZX-diagram, simplifies it to a graph-like normal form
(local complementation and pivoting remove interior Clifford spiders), gadgetizes phases so non-Clifford
phases on the same parity meet and fuse across Hadamards ("phase teleportation"), then extracts a circuit.
Phase teleportation does not change the number or location of non-phase gates; it also works with arbitrary
and symbolic phases. The same simplifier often proves the optimized circuit equal to the original.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T or Clifford+Rz circuit; strongest where Hadamards split phase
polynomials into regions that phase folding alone cannot merge (Toffoli-heavy arithmetic). It cannot
introduce ancillas or measurements, so it stays at the unitary T-count (e.g. 8n for ripple-carry adders).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count in our runs; no ancillas, no measurements. Extraction can increase CNOT
count (TKET / basic_optimization help).

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving). Self-check: `zx.Circuit.verify_equality`; the project
re-checks every output independently (dense unitary / statevector / sparse basis pairs).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/bench_runs/run2/`, pyzx 0.10.7, full_reduce -> extract_circuit ->
to_basic_gates -> basic_optimization).** tof_3: 21 -> 15 T; adder_8: 399 -> 173 T; cuccaro_4: 56 -> 32 T;
all verified against the input. The paper's Table 1 (arXiv:1903.10477v2 p.4) lists 15 for tof3 and 173 for
adder8 (PyZX column).

**Citation.** A. Kissinger, J. van de Wetering, "Reducing the number of non-Clifford gates in quantum
circuits", *Phys. Rev. A* 102, 022406 (2020), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.102.022406, arXiv:1903.10477 (arXiv title:
"Reducing T-count with the ZX-calculus").

### 07_phase_folding_tpar
# Phase folding and T-par (Amy, Maslov, Mosca 2014)

**What it does.** Inside a {CNOT, X, T, S, Z} region every phase gate applies omega^k to a parity (XOR of
input variables) of the region's inputs: the region is a phase polynomial plus a linear reversible map.
Terms on the same parity merge (T + T = S, T + T^dagger = I), which cuts T-count ("phase folding"); T-par then
re-synthesizes each region, grouping parities into T layers by matroid partitioning to minimize T-depth,
optionally with ancillas. Hadamard gates bound the regions.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T circuit with repeated parities across CNOT networks: expanded
Toffoli cascades (each 7-T Toffoli is 7 parity terms), adders, GF(2^n) multipliers, Hamming / hwb circuits.
Also on Clifford+Rz with arbitrary angles (merge angles on equal parities).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count; no ancillas or measurements for T-count reduction (ancillas only for
T-depth). Reported on its benchmarks: up to 65.7 % T-count and 87.6 % T-depth reduction without ancillae.

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving; D[omega] check of the rewritten window).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`, key `phase_folding_parity`).**
`cx(0,1) t(1) cx(0,1)` and `cx(1,0) t(0) cx(1,0)` both put T on parity x0+x1; the two terms fold into S on
that parity: 2 T -> 0 T (pyzx), dense-unitary distance 1e-16. The project already has a deterministic
phase-folding pass (`circuitevolve/blocks/passes.py`).

**Citation.** M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, "Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits
via matroid partitioning", *IEEE Trans. Comput.-Aided Des. Integr. Circuits Syst.* 33(10), 1476-1489 (2014),
doi:10.1109/TCAD.2014.2341953, arXiv:1303.2042.

### 02_jones_toffoli_measurement
# Toffoli with 4 T via measurement (Jones 2013)

**What it does.** Implements a full Toffoli `ccx(a, b, c)` with Clifford operations plus four T gates
instead of seven: compute `a AND b` into one clean ancilla (4 T), CNOT the ancilla onto `c`, then erase the
ancilla by X-basis measurement and a classically controlled CZ(a, b). Jones also shows that adding n
control inputs to a controlled gate costs 4n T (best prior 8n), and gives an error-detecting 8-T Toffoli
variant (post-selection suppresses error from 4p to 28p^2 to lowest order).

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Toffoli whose target is not a fresh ancilla (in-place targets, e.g.
the final Toffoli of a tof_n ladder, MAJ/UMA steps of a Cuccaro adder) when one clean ancilla is available.
Equivalent to card 01 used as compute + CNOT + uncompute.

**Cost.** 4 T, 1 clean ancilla, 1 measurement, 1 classically controlled CZ per Toffoli (vs 7 T, 0 ancillas).
T-depth can be 1 with the AND written in T-depth-one form (card 04).

**Verification mode: relaxed.** Uses an ancilla precondition and a measurement; check with the
specification contract (invariant 2), not unitary equality.

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`).** Standard Toffoli `ir._CCX`: 7 T, 6 CX,
distance 3e-33 to CCX (`toffoli_7T`). The 4-T AND gadget and its measurement uncompute are verified under
`temporary_and`; the Jones Toffoli is AND -> CX(anc, c) -> uncompute = 4 T (`jones_toffoli`, derived count).
In the suite: every ccz in tof_n / barenco_tof_n / adders is a candidate (MANIFEST.csv `ccx_count`).

**Citation.** C. Jones, "Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate",
*Phys. Rev. A* 87, 022328 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.87.022328, arXiv:1212.5069 (arXiv title: "Novel
constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate").

### 08_pyzx_zx_simplification
# ZX-calculus T-count reduction / phase teleportation (Kissinger & van de Wetering 2020)

**What it does.** Converts the circuit to a ZX-diagram, simplifies it to a graph-like normal form
(local complementation and pivoting remove interior Clifford spiders), gadgetizes phases so non-Clifford
phases on the same parity meet and fuse across Hadamards ("phase teleportation"), then extracts a circuit.
Phase teleportation does not change the number or location of non-phase gates; it also works with arbitrary
and symbolic phases. The same simplifier often proves the optimized circuit equal to the original.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T or Clifford+Rz circuit; strongest where Hadamards split phase
polynomials into regions that phase folding alone cannot merge (Toffoli-heavy arithmetic). It cannot
introduce ancillas or measurements, so it stays at the unitary T-count (e.g. 8n for ripple-carry adders).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count in our runs; no ancillas, no measurements. Extraction can increase CNOT
count (TKET / basic_optimization help).

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving). Self-check: `zx.Circuit.verify_equality`; the project
re-checks every output independently (dense unitary / statevector / sparse basis pairs).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/bench_runs/run2/`, pyzx 0.10.7, full_reduce -> extract_circuit ->
to_basic_gates -> basic_optimization).** tof_3: 21 -> 15 T; adder_8: 399 -> 173 T; cuccaro_4: 56 -> 32 T;
all verified against the input. The paper's Table 1 (arXiv:1903.10477v2 p.4) lists 15 for tof3 and 173 for
adder8 (PyZX column).

**Citation.** A. Kissinger, J. van de Wetering, "Reducing the number of non-Clifford gates in quantum
circuits", *Phys. Rev. A* 102, 022406 (2020), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.102.022406, arXiv:1903.10477 (arXiv title:
"Reducing T-count with the ZX-calculus").

### 07_phase_folding_tpar
# Phase folding and T-par (Amy, Maslov, Mosca 2014)

**What it does.** Inside a {CNOT, X, T, S, Z} region every phase gate applies omega^k to a parity (XOR of
input variables) of the region's inputs: the region is a phase polynomial plus a linear reversible map.
Terms on the same parity merge (T + T = S, T + T^dagger = I), which cuts T-count ("phase folding"); T-par then
re-synthesizes each region, grouping parities into T layers by matroid partitioning to minimize T-depth,
optionally with ancillas. Hadamard gates bound the regions.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T circuit with repeated parities across CNOT networks: expanded
Toffoli cascades (each 7-T Toffoli is 7 parity terms), adders, GF(2^n) multipliers, Hamming / hwb circuits.
Also on Clifford+Rz with arbitrary angles (merge angles on equal parities).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count; no ancillas or measurements for T-count reduction (ancillas only for
T-depth). Reported on its benchmarks: up to 65.7 % T-count and 87.6 % T-depth reduction without ancillae.

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving; D[omega] check of the rewritten window).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`, key `phase_folding_parity`).**
`cx(0,1) t(1) cx(0,1)` and `cx(1,0) t(0) cx(1,0)` both put T on parity x0+x1; the two terms fold into S on
that parity: 2 T -> 0 T (pyzx), dense-unitary distance 1e-16. The project already has a deterministic
phase-folding pass (`circuitevolve/blocks/passes.py`).

**Citation.** M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, "Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits
via matroid partitioning", *IEEE Trans. Comput.-Aided Des. Integr. Circuits Syst.* 33(10), 1476-1489 (2014),
doi:10.1109/TCAD.2014.2341953, arXiv:1303.2042.

### 02_jones_toffoli_measurement
# Toffoli with 4 T via measurement (Jones 2013)

**What it does.** Implements a full Toffoli `ccx(a, b, c)` with Clifford operations plus four T gates
instead of seven: compute `a AND b` into one clean ancilla (4 T), CNOT the ancilla onto `c`, then erase the
ancilla by X-basis measurement and a classically controlled CZ(a, b). Jones also shows that adding n
control inputs to a controlled gate costs 4n T (best prior 8n), and gives an error-detecting 8-T Toffoli
variant (post-selection suppresses error from 4p to 28p^2 to lowest order).

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Toffoli whose target is not a fresh ancilla (in-place targets, e.g.
the final Toffoli of a tof_n ladder, MAJ/UMA steps of a Cuccaro adder) when one clean ancilla is available.
Equivalent to card 01 used as compute + CNOT + uncompute.

**Cost.** 4 T, 1 clean ancilla, 1 measurement, 1 classically controlled CZ per Toffoli (vs 7 T, 0 ancillas).
T-depth can be 1 with the AND written in T-depth-one form (card 04).

**Verification mode: relaxed.** Uses an ancilla precondition and a measurement; check with the
specification contract (invariant 2), not unitary equality.

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`).** Standard Toffoli `ir._CCX`: 7 T, 6 CX,
distance 3e-33 to CCX (`toffoli_7T`). The 4-T AND gadget and its measurement uncompute are verified under
`temporary_and`; the Jones Toffoli is AND -> CX(anc, c) -> uncompute = 4 T (`jones_toffoli`, derived count).
In the suite: every ccz in tof_n / barenco_tof_n / adders is a candidate (MANIFEST.csv `ccx_count`).

**Citation.** C. Jones, "Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate",
*Phys. Rev. A* 87, 022328 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.87.022328, arXiv:1212.5069 (arXiv title: "Novel
constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate").

### 08_pyzx_zx_simplification
# ZX-calculus T-count reduction / phase teleportation (Kissinger & van de Wetering 2020)

**What it does.** Converts the circuit to a ZX-diagram, simplifies it to a graph-like normal form
(local complementation and pivoting remove interior Clifford spiders), gadgetizes phases so non-Clifford
phases on the same parity meet and fuse across Hadamards ("phase teleportation"), then extracts a circuit.
Phase teleportation does not change the number or location of non-phase gates; it also works with arbitrary
and symbolic phases. The same simplifier often proves the optimized circuit equal to the original.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T or Clifford+Rz circuit; strongest where Hadamards split phase
polynomials into regions that phase folding alone cannot merge (Toffoli-heavy arithmetic). It cannot
introduce ancillas or measurements, so it stays at the unitary T-count (e.g. 8n for ripple-carry adders).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count in our runs; no ancillas, no measurements. Extraction can increase CNOT
count (TKET / basic_optimization help).

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving). Self-check: `zx.Circuit.verify_equality`; the project
re-checks every output independently (dense unitary / statevector / sparse basis pairs).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/bench_runs/run2/`, pyzx 0.10.7, full_reduce -> extract_circuit ->
to_basic_gates -> basic_optimization).** tof_3: 21 -> 15 T; adder_8: 399 -> 173 T; cuccaro_4: 56 -> 32 T;
all verified against the input. The paper's Table 1 (arXiv:1903.10477v2 p.4) lists 15 for tof3 and 173 for
adder8 (PyZX column).

**Citation.** A. Kissinger, J. van de Wetering, "Reducing the number of non-Clifford gates in quantum
circuits", *Phys. Rev. A* 102, 022406 (2020), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.102.022406, arXiv:1903.10477 (arXiv title:
"Reducing T-count with the ZX-calculus").

### 07_phase_folding_tpar
# Phase folding and T-par (Amy, Maslov, Mosca 2014)

**What it does.** Inside a {CNOT, X, T, S, Z} region every phase gate applies omega^k to a parity (XOR of
input variables) of the region's inputs: the region is a phase polynomial plus a linear reversible map.
Terms on the same parity merge (T + T = S, T + T^dagger = I), which cuts T-count ("phase folding"); T-par then
re-synthesizes each region, grouping parities into T layers by matroid partitioning to minimize T-depth,
optionally with ancillas. Hadamard gates bound the regions.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T circuit with repeated parities across CNOT networks: expanded
Toffoli cascades (each 7-T Toffoli is 7 parity terms), adders, GF(2^n) multipliers, Hamming / hwb circuits.
Also on Clifford+Rz with arbitrary angles (merge angles on equal parities).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count; no ancillas or measurements for T-count reduction (ancillas only for
T-depth). Reported on its benchmarks: up to 65.7 % T-count and 87.6 % T-depth reduction without ancillae.

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving; D[omega] check of the rewritten window).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`, key `phase_folding_parity`).**
`cx(0,1) t(1) cx(0,1)` and `cx(1,0) t(0) cx(1,0)` both put T on parity x0+x1; the two terms fold into S on
that parity: 2 T -> 0 T (pyzx), dense-unitary distance 1e-16. The project already has a deterministic
phase-folding pass (`circuitevolve/blocks/passes.py`).

**Citation.** M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, "Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits
via matroid partitioning", *IEEE Trans. Comput.-Aided Des. Integr. Circuits Syst.* 33(10), 1476-1489 (2014),
doi:10.1109/TCAD.2014.2341953, arXiv:1303.2042.

### 02_jones_toffoli_measurement
# Toffoli with 4 T via measurement (Jones 2013)

**What it does.** Implements a full Toffoli `ccx(a, b, c)` with Clifford operations plus four T gates
instead of seven: compute `a AND b` into one clean ancilla (4 T), CNOT the ancilla onto `c`, then erase the
ancilla by X-basis measurement and a classically controlled CZ(a, b). Jones also shows that adding n
control inputs to a controlled gate costs 4n T (best prior 8n), and gives an error-detecting 8-T Toffoli
variant (post-selection suppresses error from 4p to 28p^2 to lowest order).

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Toffoli whose target is not a fresh ancilla (in-place targets, e.g.
the final Toffoli of a tof_n ladder, MAJ/UMA steps of a Cuccaro adder) when one clean ancilla is available.
Equivalent to card 01 used as compute + CNOT + uncompute.

**Cost.** 4 T, 1 clean ancilla, 1 measurement, 1 classically controlled CZ per Toffoli (vs 7 T, 0 ancillas).
T-depth can be 1 with the AND written in T-depth-one form (card 04).

**Verification mode: relaxed.** Uses an ancilla precondition and a measurement; check with the
specification contract (invariant 2), not unitary equality.

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`).** Standard Toffoli `ir._CCX`: 7 T, 6 CX,
distance 3e-33 to CCX (`toffoli_7T`). The 4-T AND gadget and its measurement uncompute are verified under
`temporary_and`; the Jones Toffoli is AND -> CX(anc, c) -> uncompute = 4 T (`jones_toffoli`, derived count).
In the suite: every ccz in tof_n / barenco_tof_n / adders is a candidate (MANIFEST.csv `ccx_count`).

**Citation.** C. Jones, "Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate",
*Phys. Rev. A* 87, 022328 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.87.022328, arXiv:1212.5069 (arXiv title: "Novel
constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate").

### 08_pyzx_zx_simplification
# ZX-calculus T-count reduction / phase teleportation (Kissinger & van de Wetering 2020)

**What it does.** Converts the circuit to a ZX-diagram, simplifies it to a graph-like normal form
(local complementation and pivoting remove interior Clifford spiders), gadgetizes phases so non-Clifford
phases on the same parity meet and fuse across Hadamards ("phase teleportation"), then extracts a circuit.
Phase teleportation does not change the number or location of non-phase gates; it also works with arbitrary
and symbolic phases. The same simplifier often proves the optimized circuit equal to the original.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T or Clifford+Rz circuit; strongest where Hadamards split phase
polynomials into regions that phase folding alone cannot merge (Toffoli-heavy arithmetic). It cannot
introduce ancillas or measurements, so it stays at the unitary T-count (e.g. 8n for ripple-carry adders).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count in our runs; no ancillas, no measurements. Extraction can increase CNOT
count (TKET / basic_optimization help).

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving). Self-check: `zx.Circuit.verify_equality`; the project
re-checks every output independently (dense unitary / statevector / sparse basis pairs).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/bench_runs/run2/`, pyzx 0.10.7, full_reduce -> extract_circuit ->
to_basic_gates -> basic_optimization).** tof_3: 21 -> 15 T; adder_8: 399 -> 173 T; cuccaro_4: 56 -> 32 T;
all verified against the input. The paper's Table 1 (arXiv:1903.10477v2 p.4) lists 15 for tof3 and 173 for
adder8 (PyZX column).

**Citation.** A. Kissinger, J. van de Wetering, "Reducing the number of non-Clifford gates in quantum
circuits", *Phys. Rev. A* 102, 022406 (2020), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.102.022406, arXiv:1903.10477 (arXiv title:
"Reducing T-count with the ZX-calculus").

### 07_phase_folding_tpar
# Phase folding and T-par (Amy, Maslov, Mosca 2014)

**What it does.** Inside a {CNOT, X, T, S, Z} region every phase gate applies omega^k to a parity (XOR of
input variables) of the region's inputs: the region is a phase polynomial plus a linear reversible map.
Terms on the same parity merge (T + T = S, T + T^dagger = I), which cuts T-count ("phase folding"); T-par then
re-synthesizes each region, grouping parities into T layers by matroid partitioning to minimize T-depth,
optionally with ancillas. Hadamard gates bound the regions.

**When it applies (pattern).** Any Clifford+T circuit with repeated parities across CNOT networks: expanded
Toffoli cascades (each 7-T Toffoli is 7 parity terms), adders, GF(2^n) multipliers, Hamming / hwb circuits.
Also on Clifford+Rz with arbitrary angles (merge angles on equal parities).

**Cost.** Never increases T-count; no ancillas or measurements for T-count reduction (ancillas only for
T-depth). Reported on its benchmarks: up to 65.7 % T-count and 87.6 % T-depth reduction without ancillae.

**Verification mode: exact** (unitary-preserving; D[omega] check of the rewritten window).

**Worked example (run: `results/v2/cards_worked_examples.json`, key `phase_folding_parity`).**
`cx(0,1) t(1) cx(0,1)` and `cx(1,0) t(0) cx(1,0)` both put T on parity x0+x1; the two terms fold into S on
that parity: 2 T -> 0 T (pyzx), dense-unitary distance 1e-16. The project already has a deterministic
phase-folding pass (`circuitevolve/blocks/passes.py`).

**Citation.** M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, "Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits
via matroid partitioning", *IEEE Trans. Comput.-Aided Des. Integr. Circuits Syst.* 33(10), 1476-1489 (2014),
doi:10.1109/TCAD.2014.2341953, arXiv:1303.2042.
